name: W27 Morning Flow — Bodyweight Spine + Hip (All Days, Rotated Variety)
description:
The daily 15-minute opener. This week rotates roughly half the moves again: the primer goes to **world's greatest stretch, down-dog knee-to-head and the hip-flexor lunge**, the work block trades in **bird-dog, side plank and plié-relevé**, and the yoga arc closes on **saddle pose and a straddle sit**. Anchors stay put: scorpion, lizard, cossack, the push-up greasing set, and the rehab cluster in the day-specific add-on.

**Two of this week's moves are chosen for what your days look like now.** The side plank is anti-lateral-flexion work — the exact thing that resists carrying a baby on one hip for an hour. The hip-flexor lunge and saddle pose undo the sitting and the low reaching.

**This flow is also your readiness screen.** The cossacks have called the quality of a session before it started more reliably than sleep quality has. Pay attention to them, especially in a week where sleep is a new variable.

**Order is deliberate.** Primer wakes the spine, work block warms the body, and the deep stretch arc goes last because warm muscle stretches further. Do not reorder it to get the stretching over with.

sets.name: Primer — Wake the Spine (~3 min)
sets.notes: Slow and unhurried. You just got out of bed — this is about getting the spine and hips to agree to move, not about a stimulus.

exercises.notes: 45s each side. Lunge, elbow to the instep, then rotate and reach for the ceiling. **It earns the name** — hip flexor, adductor, thoracic spine and shoulder in one shape. Let the back knee stay off the floor if the hip allows.

30s each side. From down dog, draw one knee toward the forehead and round the spine, then extend the leg back and up. **Move between the two rather than holding either** — this is the flowing part of the primer.
30s each side. Half-kneeling, **tuck the pelvis under before leaning forward** — without the tuck this stretches the low back instead of the hip flexor. Undoes the sitting and the low reaching.

sets.name: Work Block — Bodyweight Activation (~5 min)
sets.notes: Warm the body. **Activate, do not fatigue** — this precedes a gym session most days.

exercises.notes: **The greasing set — one quick set, never to failure.** Elbows ~45°, **pack down not up**. This is a daily habit, not a training stimulus.
Opposite arm and leg, **hips completely level** — a glass of water on the low back should not spill. Reach long rather than lifting high. Slow, deliberate, 2s hold at the extension.

30s each side. **Anti-lateral-flexion work — the direct counter to carrying a baby on one hip.** Stack the shoulders and hips, drive the bottom hip up, neck long. Drop to the knee if the top-end shape breaks.
Wide second position, heels lift as the knees bend. **Slow and controlled through the ankle** — this is calf and foot work as much as legs, and the ankle is part of the squat-depth question.

sets.name: Yoga Flow — Deep Stretch Arc (~7 min)
sets.notes: **One continuous arc, not five separate holds.** Move from shape to shape and let the body be warm by the time it gets to the deep hip work at the end. Breathe slowly throughout.

exercises.notes: 30s each side. Prone, reach the foot across. Thoracic rotation and hip flexor together.
45s each side. Deep lunge, both hands inside the front foot. Drop to the forearms if the hip allows.
**Your readiness screen.** Slow, deep, heel down. How these feel today tells you what kind of session you are walking into.
Kneeling, lean back as far as the quads allow — forearms, or all the way down. **Come out slowly.** Deep quad and hip flexor work, and a direct undo for the hours of sitting.
Wide legs, **hinge from the hips with a long spine** rather than rounding to reach further. Walk the hands forward and centre, then to each side. Finish here.

sets.name: 📍 Day-Specific Add-On — Pick by Today's Training (~3-5 min)
sets.notes: **The rehab cluster — these are anchors and they do not rotate.** Take the ones that fit today: shoulder work before push and pull, hip work before legs, and the dead hang whenever the shoulders feel compressed.

exercises.notes: **Push and pull days.** 30s each arm, elbow at MID height.
**Rehab anchor.** Thumbs up, arms in a Y. Lift from the mid-back, not the neck.
**Rehab anchor.** Plank position, only the shoulder blades move. Protract and retract.
**Rehab anchor.** Elbow pinned to the ribs, light or no weight. Slow.
**Rehab anchor.** Back flat to the wall, arms slide up and down. Keep the wrists in contact.
**Rehab anchor.** Passive. Highest value on pull days and after a night of holding a baby.
**Rehab anchor.** Hanging, shoulders pull down without the elbows bending.
**Legs days.** 30s each side. QL and psoas.
**Legs days.** 45s each side.
**Any day.** 30s each side. Good closer if the low back is tight.

tips: The cossacks are the readiness screen — trust them over how much you slept.
Work block before stretches. Warm muscle stretches deeper.
The push-up set is greasing, never a max effort.
